# Alignment

Testing addresses for alignment and rounding them to a boundary.

<h2 id="is-aligned"><code>IsAligned</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsAligned(address: uint, alignment: uint) -> bool
```

Whether `address` is a multiple of `alignment`.
`address` and `alignment` are read by value. An `alignment` of zero reports false rather than dividing by it, and
an alignment that is not a power of two gives an answer that is arithmetically true but rarely meaningful, since
hardware alignment is always a power of two.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Access.rux#L22)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type   | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `address`   | `uint` | the address or offset to test                    |
| `alignment` | `uint` | the boundary to test against; zero reports false |

**Returns**: whether `address` is a multiple of `alignment`

<h2 id="is-pointer-aligned"><code>IsPointerAligned</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsPointerAligned(
    pointer: *opaque,
    alignment: uint
) -> bool
```

Whether `pointer` is aligned for `alignment`.
`pointer` is read by value and never dereferenced. A null pointer reports true for every alignment, since zero is
a multiple of everything; a caller that means "usable" has to ask that separately.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Access.rux#L35)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description                             |
| ----------- | --------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `pointer`   | `*opaque` | the address to test, never dereferenced |
| `alignment` | `uint`    | the boundary to test against            |

**Returns**: whether `pointer` is a multiple of `alignment`

<h2 id="align-up"><code>AlignUp</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AlignUp(value: uint, alignment: uint) -> uint
```

The next multiple of `alignment` at or above `value`.
`value` and `alignment` are read by value. An `alignment` of zero or one returns `value` unchanged, since every
value is already a multiple of both.
Returns `value` itself when it is already aligned, so this is idempotent.
A `value` within `alignment - 1` of the maximum has no next multiple, and this wraps to a small number rather
than reporting it. A caller sizing an allocation must check for that before trusting the result; [`AlignUpChecked`](/docs/api/memory/alignment#align-up-checked)
does the checking.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Access.rux#L50)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type   | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `uint` | the value to round up                                 |
| `alignment` | `uint` | the boundary to round to; zero or one changes nothing |

**Returns**: the next multiple of `alignment` at or above `value`

<h2 id="align-up-checked"><code>AlignUpChecked</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AlignUpChecked(
    value: uint,
    alignment: uint,
    result: *var uint
) -> bool
```

The next multiple of `alignment` at or above `value`, reporting whether it was representable.
`value` and `alignment` are read by value; `result` receives the aligned value when this returns `false`, and is
left unwritten when it returns `true`. `result` must not be null.
Returns `true` when rounding up would pass the maximum, which is the case an allocation size has to notice: a
wrapped size is an allocation far smaller than the caller asked for.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Access.rux#L67)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `uint`      | the value to round up                                 |
| `alignment` | `uint`      | the boundary to round to; zero or one changes nothing |
| `result`    | `*var uint` | receives the aligned value when this returns false    |

**Returns**: true when rounding up would pass the maximum

<h2 id="align-down"><code>AlignDown</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AlignDown(value: uint, alignment: uint) -> uint
```

The previous multiple of `alignment` at or below `value`.
`value` and `alignment` are read by value. An `alignment` of zero or one returns `value` unchanged.
Cannot fail: rounding down never leaves the range.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Memory/Src/Access.rux#L90)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type   | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `uint` | the value to round down                               |
| `alignment` | `uint` | the boundary to round to; zero or one changes nothing |

**Returns**: the previous multiple of `alignment` at or below `value`
